key_insight: SpecEyes reduces the sequential 'agentic depth' of multimodal agent loops by speculatively precomputing likely perception outputs and planning steps, allowing perception, reasoning, and tool calls to run in parallel and be verified afterwards.
problem_solved: Agentic MLLMs pay high latency and low system concurrency due to iterative perception→reasoning→tool-calling loops (agentic depth). SpecEyes addresses this bottleneck by breaking the strict sequential dependency.
method: Speculative perception: predict likely future visual queries/regions and pre-extract features or invoke perception tools in advance.
Speculative planning: generate probable next actions/plans and pre-execute corresponding tool calls or computations in parallel.
Confidence-aware verification and rollback: validate speculative results against the agent's actual decisions and correct or discard mispredictions to preserve correctness.
impact: SpecEyes cuts end-to-end latency and increases concurrency for agentic multimodal systems, enabling more responsive, higher-throughput AI agents in real-world interactive and time-sensitive applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: sequential agent loop vs. SpecEyes speculative parallel loop (with prefetch arrows).
Timeline/latency bar chart: per-step latency comparison showing reduced critical path and lower end-to-end response time.
Speculation flowchart: prediction → parallel precompute → verification/rollback with confidence scores.
Throughput/concurrency chart: number of concurrent agent sessions or tool calls before vs. after SpecEyes.
paper_title: SpecEyes: Accelerating Agentic Multimodal LLMs via Speculative Perception and Planning
paper_authors: Haoyu Huang, Jinfa Huang, Zhongwei Wan, Xiawu Zheng, Rongrong Ji
